title: The July 20th Plot to Assassinate Hitler
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the July 20, 1944 plot (Operation Valkyrie) to assassinate Hitler. They cover the many earlier assassination attempts, the motives of the conspirators, Germany's deteriorating war position after Normandy, the peace feelers via Allen Dulles, and Operation Valkyrie as a Reserve Army contingency plan co-opted by the plotters. They describe Claus von Stauffenberg's bomb at the Wolf's Lair on July 20, the table that shielded Hitler, the delayed and chaotic response in Berlin, the failed coup, the executions, and the Sippenhaft reprisals against families. The episode also includes a listener mail segment about neuroendocrine tumor treatment and a shout-out to Mia.

segments.title: Intro and fifteen-plus Hitler assassination plots
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open by discussing why so many plots to kill Hitler failed, the Valkyrie film and Tom Cruise casting, and the conspirators' motives.

segments.title: Germany's war position and peace feelers
segments.summary: The hosts explain that by mid-1944 Germany could not win the war after Normandy, Italy was lost, and conspirators explored negotiating peace through Allen Dulles, though the Russians were excluded from talks.

segments.title: Nazi control, Sippenhaft, and Operation Valkyrie
segments.summary: Hitler's control over media and oaths, the ancient Sippenhaft family-punishment custom, and the explanation that Operation Valkyrie was an existing Reserve Army contingency plan co-opted by the plotters.

segments.title: Conspirators and Stauffenberg's background
segments.summary: Discussion of Tresckow's role in the film, Friedrich Olbricht and Fromm's cowardice, Claus von Stauffenberg's war wounds, and his brother Bertold's confession.

segments.title: The Wolf's Lair bomb on July 20
segments.summary: Stauffenberg brings two briefcase bombs to the Wolf's Lair; the meeting moves to a wooden hut, one briefcase is moved behind a heavy oak table leg by Heinz Brandt, and the bomb explodes but Hitler survives. Stauffenberg flees to Berlin.

segments.title: Failed coup in Berlin and executions
segments.summary: Delays in Berlin, confusion over whether Hitler was dead, Fromm's attempt to switch sides and arrest the plotters, the shootout at the War Ministry, Stauffenberg's execution, and the People's Court under Freisler.

segments.title: Reprisals, suicides, and aftermath
segments.summary: Around seven thousand arrested and five thousand executed, Sippenhaft reprisals against families, Rommel forced to take cyanide, and Bertold von Stauffenberg's execution by strangulation on a meat hook.

segments.title: Listener mail: neuroendocrine tumor and Mia
segments.summary: Listener Bo Miller writes about his wife Mia's neuroendocrine tumor treatment (PRRT) in Salt Lake City, noting the common misreporting as pancreatic cancer, and asks for a shout-out. Also thanks for art sent by Lawson Barney and Alison Gallagher.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode and point listeners to the website and email.
